headline: Approved an 83-unit apartment complex at 110 Leigus Road with conditions, including an $8,000 bond and a wetland fence.
summary: A public hearing covered the proposed 83-unit apartment complex at 110 Leigus Road, including wetlands, stormwater, and a proposed conservation area. The project was approved with conditions by a 5-0 vote. Repairs to the landfill cap at 528 South Cherry Street were also approved with conditions.

Approved application #A26-7.1 at 110 Leigus Road with conditions, including an $8,000 bond, 5-0.
Deemed application #A26-7.2 at 528 South Cherry Street not a significant impact activity, 5-0.
Approved application #A26-7.2 at 528 South Cherry Street with conditions, including a $10,000 sediment and erosion control bond, 5-0.
Tabled application #A26-7.6 for a parking lot expansion at 358 Hall Avenue.
Tabled the bond release request for 59 North Elm Street Carr Hall.
Approved the transfer of Permit #A24-10.2 for 231 New Cheshire Road to a new name, by voice vote.
Released the violation and bond for #A19-3.6 at 988 East Center Street, by voice vote.

Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, October 7, 2026  Page 1 
Wallingford Inland Wetlands and Watercourses Commission 
 
Regular Meeting 
Wednesday, October 7 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Room  
Town Hall – 45 South Main Street, Wallingford, CT 
 
MINUTES 
 
Chair James Vitali called this Regular Meeting of the Wallingford Inland Wetlands and Watercourses 
Commission to order on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. in the Robert F. Parisi Council 
Chambers, Town Hall, 45 South Main Street, Wallingford, CT. 
 
PRESENT: Chair Vitali, Secretary Nick Kern, Commissioner Michael Caruso, and Alternate Commissioners 
James Heilman, Aili McKeen, Caroline Raynis and Sebastian Velez, Environmental and Natural Resources 
Planner. 
 
ABSENT: Vice Chair, Debbie Phillips and Commissioner Jeffrey Necio. 
 
A. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
The Pledge was recited. 
 
B. ROLL CALL 
As above. 
 
Chair Vitali stated that the voters tonight would be Commissioners Kern, Caruso, Heilman, McKeen and 
himself. 
 
C. CONSIDERATION OF MINUTES 
1. Regular Meeting, September 2, 2026, 7:00 p.m. (corrected) 
 
MR. CARUSO: MOTION TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF SEPTEMBER 2,  
  2026  
   
MS. MCKEEN: SECOND. 
VOTE:  MR. CARUSO – YES; MR. KERN – YES;  MR. HEILMAN – YES; MS. MCKEEN – YES;  
  CHAIR VITALI – YES.  
 
Chair Vitali read a statement providing an overview of the Commission’s role and responsibilities and 
the types of comments that are appropriate. It included the statement that Commission decisions must 
be based strictly on environmental factors, including potential impacts to natural resources, water 
quality, wildlife habitat and overall ecosystem function. 
 
D. OLD BUSINESS 
1.  PUBLIC HEARING #A26-7.1 /110 Leigus Road – Metro Realty – (Multi-family apartment 
complex (83 units) with associated parking area under CT Statute 8-30g) 
 
Chair Vitali noted the public hearing opened as of 7:07 pm.
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, October 7, 2026  Page 2 
Appearing were Atty. Andrea Gomes, Hinkley Allen, 20 Church Street, Hartford; Kyle Richards, Executive 
Vice President, Metro Realty; Tom Daly, Consulting Civil Engineer with SLR; and Matt Sanford, Wetland 
and Soil Scientist with SLR. 
 
Atty. Gomes stated that all notification requirements for the public hearing have been met. 
 
Chair Vitali stated that the applicant requested the public hearing. 
 
Mr. Richards used a PowerPoint presentation to introduced Metro Realty and its track record.  He stated 
that they take maintenance very seriously and have more than 25 staff to manage the communities and 
the stormwater management systems.  The company has not received a citation from a town on 
maintenance in their 30 year history. He pointed out the 21.5 acre parcel formerly labeled Lot C.  All 
access will be from Miles Drive.  The development will be on a previously cleared area with no direct 
wetlands impact.  They will gift to the Town 11.3 acres to be permanently conserved.  They have met 
with Wallingford Land Trust about ownership and walking trails. The company is committed to 
permanently conserving these 11.3 acres. How it will be done is up to the Town. 
 
Mr. Daly stated that the overall campus is approved for subdivision but their proposed site plan is 
confined to the existing former farm field. The woods and wetlands will not be impacted.  He showed 
where the watercourse is in the wooded area.  He showed the existing sanitary sewer.  There is a stone 
wall separating the wooded portion from the cleared portion.  They will stay on the cleared side of the 
wall. He showed the site plan with the dedicated right of way, distributed parking close to front doors 
and sidewalks throughout.  He explained the landscape plan. He described the locations of the two 
regulated activity areas. One is in the north end of the property.  The hotel discharge goes across the 
property line. They will pick up the drainage pipe and move it to the other side of the driveway. This will 
occur in an upland review area.  There will be a small amount of grading in the upland review area.  A 
total of approximately 1000 sq. ft. is affected.  The second area is in the south end of the development 
at the driveway turn around.  This will be in an upland area adjacent to a wetland pocket.  They have 
designed a retaining wall with a fence to minimize activity in the wetland.  He described the proposed 
fence as an agricultural style that will restrict debris from the site from going into the restricted area.  He 
suggested deferring construction of the fence until the need is determined. They are willing to have this 
as a condition. The wall will be 21 ft. away from the wetland.  Approximately 5,000 sq. ft. of regulated 
area is affected. He described the stormwater drainage system which will be in the southern end of the 
property. This is in the Watershed Protection Zone so there are higher standards for water quality.  The 
basin will not be in the upland review area or wetland area.  Ultimately the discharge will go into the 
upland review area.  The design meets the town and DEEP regulations. Water & Sewer and the Town 
Engineer have approved the design. He reviewed the Erosion Control plan.  He reported that the 
neighbors requested the permanent protection of the wetlands and upland review area.  Over 50% of 
the site will be in permanent restriction.  They are more than willing to work with the town to 
accomplish this.   
 
Mr. Sanford reviewed the two existing wetlands systems and soil functions and values.  One is a wet 
meadow to forested wetland and is near the western property line. It includes a series of intermittent 
watercourses that converge to become a perennial watercourse that goes into the Muddy River.  The 
second wetland is about .15 acre and he believes it is a manmade wetland. He reviewed how he 
determined the function and value of each wetland based on the Army Corps Highway Methodology 
workbook.  The first wetland (WA) has more principle functions and values including wildlife habitat and 
flood flow attenuation.  The smaller one (WB) has less function and value.  He reported that they looked
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, October 7, 2026  Page 3 
for potential for protected species, specifically bald eagles and northern long eared bats.  No bald eagle 
nesting sites or caves for the bats were found on the property.  He commented on the impact on the 
upland review area.  For the stormwater outfall extension, they are extending an existing pipe and will 
maintain the existing hydrology. He sees no adverse impact.  The retaining wall at the driveway turn 
around will be within the 50 ft. review area of the smaller wetland but will be 21 ft. from the wetland 
edge.  With the natural vegetative plantings, he sees no adverse affect.  He stated that the existing stone 
wall will be preserved and the large trees protected.  The proposed conservation restriction will protect 
both wetland areas.  
 
Chair Vitali asked about the fence installation at the end of the project.  Mr. Richards replied that they 
are agreeable to install it either during construction or waiting to see if it’s necessary.  Chair Vitali stated 
that it will help keep the construction people out of the upland review area.  He asked if there were any 
test pits on the profile of the ground.  Mr. Daly replied that they did them for the stormwater and have 
done a full geotechnical study of the property which found no construction issues.  Chair Vitali stated 
that on the Leigus Road side, it was found that there was heavy soil on top of gravel. This affected 
drainage.  Mr. Daly replied that they did find layers, but not like that. Chair Vitali stated a potential for 
lack of water retention if there is gravel underneath.   
 
Commissioner Heilman stated that he doesn’t think this property will have the same issue.  He likes the 
idea of the fence. He’d like to see openings every 40 ft. to allow small wildlife to get through.  He stated 
that he is concerned with maintenance of the detention basin as most are not maintained.  He stated 
that this proposal protects the wetlands and the exposure to the upland review area is minimal.  He 
suggested signs to tell people that it is a wetland area.   
 
Commissioner Raynis agreed with placards on the fence.  She asked if they knew if the tree that the bats 
like is found in the woods.  Mr. Sanford replied that since they are protecting the whole area, they did 
not survey all the trees.  Ms. Raynis asked if there are any caves in the nearby area that could house the 
bats.  Mr. Sanford replied according to the CT DEEP there are none in this general vicinity.  
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
Jessica Wysocki, 76 Knollwood Drive, stated that she hikes on that property.  Allowing development on 
property adjacent to wetlands will have an impact on the wetlands.  She reminded the Commission of 
the federal Clean Water Act and the Connecticut Inland Wetlands and Watercourse Act as well as 
Wallingford’s Ordinance to protect the aquifer. 
 
Craig Fishbein, Grieb Road, stated that he agreed with adding the fence but questioned the openings.  
He stated that he is impressed by this company and the conveyance or conservation easement.  He was 
originally concerned about his well.  If the conveyance is to the Town and properties to the south are 
impacted by water runoff, they can petition the town government to do something. If it’s a conservation 
easement or a gift to the land trust, residents would have no one to complain to.  He stated that we 
need to protect people and wetlands.  He believes the best solution would be the conveyance.  He 
mentioned a petition with almost300 signatures.  Chair Vitali noted that the fence sections could 
overlap with a small opening.  Mr. Fishbein agreed with that. 
 
Ken Lloyd, President of the Wallingford Community Farmer’s Group stated that a lot of people are 
concerned about this.  You can’t contain wildlife.  The Commission is here for land, water, and the
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, October 7, 2026  Page 4 
environment.  There are empty buildings in industrial areas that could be adapted for housing.  He 
stated that a lot of people are opposed to this. 
 
State Representative Mary Mushinsky stated that she is also the Executive Director of River Advocates of 
South Central CT.  This area is former agricultural land. The proposed conservation easement (or other 
arrangement) will reduce stormwater runoff. The developer should also monitor the vegetative buffer of 
the watercourse between any developed land and any flow toward the river.  The stormwater 
management system must be maintained into the future.  Please find a way to ensure the long-term 
function of the stormwater management system. She added that bald eagles have been seen at North 
Farms Reservoir recently.  She recommended signs to mark the protected wetlands.  She noted that the 
similar project in Cheshire is energy efficient, and this will be too.  The applicant has taken care of the 
sensitive areas of the site.  This will be a good use of this former agricultural land. 
 
Commissioner Kern asked if the Town can handle maintenance of this new open space parcel.  He asked 
if the Town does not take the parcel, will the applicant maintain it. Mr. Richards replied that the idea of 
the conservation area came from the neighbors.  Metro Realty is capable and willing to maintain the 
conservation area, preserve and protect it.  They wanted to be sensitive to the wishes of the Town.  
Either way, the 11.3 acres will be permanently conserved.  Mr. Kern suggested that it be maintained put 
in writing, if the Town doesn’t take it. 
 
Commissioner Heilman asked what we want to maintain. What was the property before it was a 
meadow? Should it go back to forest?  He would like to see it conserved the way it would be naturally.  
Maintenance would is beyond our purview.  
 
Al Renda, 95 Leigus Road, stated that bald eagles are there all the time.  He stated that he doesn’t think 
the runoff or the water treatment system will work long term. If not properly maintained the system will 
fail.  There should be mandatory yearly water testing of the water coming out of these ponds. The wells 
on Grieb Road will be affected.  This needs contingencies and plans.  Who is going to be accountable? 
 
Betsey Stalato, 36 Broadview Drive, stated that Metro Realty is well established with good maintenance 
record.  There is nothing happening in that wetlands now.  Anything that happens is an improvement. 
 
Scott Amore, Jenna Road, stated that there will be zero wetlands disturbance, no new utilities to be 
added and a conservation easement.  Look at what is allowed in the zone. This is the highest and best 
use of the property. We don’t know what’s proposed for the remaining parts of this property.  Setting 
the precedent to conserve the land is something we can use for further developments. 
 
AJ Anois, part of the Fairlawn Farms Association, stated that the applicant is more than willing to 
accommodate the wishes of the Town.  He supports the project.  
 
Chair Vitali asked Commissioners for comments. 
 
Commissioner Raynis asked if the easement or whatever should be considered a condition of approval.  
 
Chair Vitali stated that the plan is to put conservation easement on the wetlands corridor. The  question 
is who will own it and maintain it.
Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission 
Regular Meeting, October 7, 2026  Page 5 
Atty. Gomes stated that they have no control over whether the Town will accept donation of the 
property. She suggested a condition requiring the ongoing preservation of the 11.3 acres shown on plan 
whether by a conservation restriction or by donation to the Town or other entity designated by the 
Town.  That way we get a little bit of flexibility but ensures that it will be preserved in its natural state.  
Regarding maintenance, there is a very big difference between maintaining a meadow versus ensuring a 
wooded area remains untouched.  She suggested an approval condition that if the Town refuses the 
donation and Metro puts a conservation restriction on that 11.3 acres, Metro Realty will work with Staff 
to create a maintenance plan to ensure it remains in its natural wooded state. 
 
Commissioner McKeen noted that they are going to build on the meadow-ish part of the property and 
the wooded part doesn’t need much maintenance.  Maintenance would be control of trash and invasive 
species.  She noted that it won’t be pleasant being right next to the highway. She would like to see a less 
dense project though it is a good use of the property.   
 
Commissioner Kern stated concern with general maintenance and oversight. 
 
Chair Vitali closed the public hearing at 8:41 pm. He asked if Commission members were ready to vote 
tonight.  Consensus was yes. 
 
Mr. Velez recommended approval with conditions. 
 
Mr. Vitali called for a motion regarding significant activity.

Wallingford Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Commission

VOTE:  MR. CARUSO – YES; MR. KERN – YES; MR. HEILMAN – YES; MS. MCKEEN – YES;

E. NEW BUSINESS 
1. #A26-7.2 / 528 South Cherry Street – Virginia Ryan, CPEA, REM – (Site clearing and remedial 
actions for waste)  
 
Amberly Clark, an Environmental consultant with WSPUSA, stated that she is representing Allnex USA, 
Inc. and noted that the applicant, Virginia Ryan, could not be here tonight.  The application includes 
temporary and permanent wetland impacts two wetlands and a stream due to existing site conditions 
and engineering constraints.  This is an older landfill that is referred to as the Powder Dump.  The landfill 
has construction and other non-hazardous waste built up in a low lying area that abuts a small stream.  
It is surrounded by three wetlands.  The purpose of the project is to fix or repair the existing landfill  cap 
and cover.  Erosion has been occurring so it needs to be capped to meet DEEP standards.  They will pull 
back the northern edge, consolidate the waste, re-grade it and cap it.  They are not removing any of the 
waste.  This will prevent additional infiltration.  There will be some tree removal and excavation in a 
limited area.  A low permeability cap will be added.  An environmental use restriction will be placed on 
the land records. An operation & maintenance plan will also be on the Land records.  This will include 
maintenance of the cap itself, mowing, any repairs, and ground water monitoring. 
 
Chair Vitali asked if this is being done voluntarily remediation per DEEP. Ms. Clark replied that the 
project has been approved by the DEEP. 
 
Mr. Velez stated that he would like to see a better drawing showing the location of the stream. Ms. 
Clark indicated the stream in the drawing lines up with the high water mark.  Mr. Velez then 
recommended approval with conditions. 
 
Mr. Vitali stated that these projects are controlling the containment from going further down into the 
soil. He called for a motion.
